turns.t: Morning, Mr Kelly, I'm Anna, I'll do your measurements first and then the doctor will see you. Shoes off, up on the scales. ~
Righto. ~
Weight 68 kilos, height 178 centimetres. Blood pressure 136 over 74, pulse 104, temperature 37.0.
Is that normal? ~
I'll leave it to the doctor to talk through. Pop in when you're ready. ~
Come in, Mr Kelly. What's brought you in? ~
I've been losing weight, doc, and I'm eating like a horse.
How much weight, and over what time?
About eight kilos since Christmas. I was seventy-six.
That's a lot. And you're eating normally, or more than normal? ~
More. I'm hungry all the time, and I've still lost it. ~
Anything else you've noticed along with it? ~
I'm sweating. Even sitting still, even in winter.
Do you smoke?
Never. Not once.
Your pulse is quicker than I'd expect when you're sitting, and I can see you've got a bit of a tremor in your hands. ~
Yeah, I noticed that. I put it down to coffee. ~
Possibly, but with the weight loss and the sweating, I'd like to check your thyroid. I'm going to arrange a blood test today.
Right. Whatever it takes. ~
The nurse will take it before you go. We'll ring you with the result in a few days. ~
Should I be worried? ~
Not yet. There are a few reasons for this, and many are easy to treat. ~
Okay. What should I do in the meantime? ~
Eat as you normally do, don't skip meals, and cut down the coffee.
That'll be hard. ~
Try one a day. ~
Fine. ~
If the weight keeps falling, or you get palpitations or a high temperature, ring us earlier.
I will. Thanks, doc. ~
I'll take that blood now, Mr Kelly, if you'd like to follow me. ~
Lead the way. ~
